speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To better understand your condition, can you describe the specific physical features you have noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

The clinical picture of ambiguous genitalia at birth, severe acne, hirsutism, and primary amenorrhea in an adolescent is highly suggestive of this condition. REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone; REQUEST TEST: ACTH stimulation test; REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic ultrasound to evaluate for ovarian morphology.
